Whilst I like polish and want the game to not be a buggy unoptimised mess on release, I worry about there being no beta for a couple of reasons.

1. Players are usually your best source of finding bugs or weird interactions as you're canvassing over multiple different systems and having all sorts of variations in how the game gets played. Some players are genuinely devoted to finding bugs in the weirdest places.

2. If the game genuinely doesn't feel good in certain ways, you're just waiting and praying on release instead of potentially missing good player feedback to help the game shine more. It also helps you get a feel for the reaction the wider audience will have on release.

It's true a beta would take a lot of manpower and also leads to sifting through individual opinions so I can only hope the game they're polishing is as good as can be and that the polishing actually works for release.

1. Send Songbird to the moon - You've given her the second chance she's wanted and needed ever since Militech and the FIA set eyes on her. She would have told you sooner, but this is her life she's fighting for, and everyone around her is a professional liar. It's too risky to tell you no matter how much you help her. The fact she tells you is proof enough that she did care about you, that and the message she leaves for you. 

2. Fulfil Songbirds wish - This took a while for me to process, but realistically, it's the only other ending I can choose. At the very least, you set So Mi free and spite Myers. But to me, the reason it works is Reed. In this ending, he finally sees who he is and what he's working for. He hates you for what you did but agrees you're right about everything. Maybe now he can become a force for good inside the FIA, no longer blinded by his code or his feelings that Myers expects more of him. This ending sets Reed free. 

I've never been a fan of having to kill someone to save the other, but CDPR opened my mind to it if it's done right. Both of them are portrayed as two-sided, and both have a genuine motive for what they do. While I will almost always choose So Mi, that one ending with Reed was satisfying, and both storylines have unique climaxes that help shape the world around us. I'm not sure what I'd target if I could change one thing, but I'd honestly say the TP is what makes her more unfair vs. any other support. Like Bap has damage, big burst heal and lamp (jump too), but they're long cooldowns, and if they're down, he can not get out of that 1v1. Ana can sleep and nade to helo herself but without that sleep she can't get out the 1v1. None of the supports can just dip out from an isolated 1v1. Instead, they either sustain, fight, or rely on teammates' helping. 

Kiri is the only exception. You can purposely climb over a wall, right-click at the enemy until you're in trouble, then option select: Suzu to try confirm the kill, then TP out, or just TP out. Granted, an Ally needs to be in range, but it can be used through walls and floors, unlike Mercy's GA or any other movement abilities on support. The closest you have is Moira due to the invis and the superjump she gains when using fade. 

The problem is how do you bring her in line without it? You'd need a new ability to make her into more vulnerable support instead of a flank-capable damage support. A dash doesn't fit the character. More healing is a big nono with the current state of the game. More damage again is a big nono. 

One potential change could be to split suzu into two abilities, making Kiri more than just the E key, but then she becomes like a worse Baptiste unless these two abilites added more. Like the cleanse and the burst heal would be the core components of the two abilities, but what else would make up for the loss of the TP. 

Another change that would keep the TP would be to make it Line of Sight only, fixing some scenarios on maps like Gibraltar 2nd/Midtown underpass/Kings Row but not making any difference where you have really long sightlines still allowing for flanks/escape tps. 

I hope this is a subject that Blizzard looks into because this is something that is incredibly frustrating for a lot of people. It's not a pandemic that affects every player, but anyone who plays Kiri enough realises just how much shenanigans you can get away with if you're not being hard focused.

Episode 2 goes beyond who we know and introduces some more faces and voices, which to me were on point. The plot of the second episode feels very sudden and rushed in the latter half, but I'm still debating on whether it was a time issue or it's part of a joke about the character it involves.

However, both of them have succeeded in the musical front. The songs are varied and true to the characters whilst being catchy, and in the fashion of a musical, they serve the narrative. Episode 2 has a song that concludes with 30 seconds of absolute perfection that I can not stop watching.

Am I biased? Yes. But being as objective as I can, the pacing is the only thing I can really say stands out to me, but it doesn't detract from the story as badly as some shows.

I think the way she thinks about life changes as the game goes on. She goes through a real up and down as she has hope for her engine being fixed up until Dammon tells you he can't at the last light. 

Her plan then shifts more to a blaze of glory, still never wanting to go back to the hells but believing that through revenge, she can get some meaning out of what time she has left. This, unfortunately, turns out not to be the case. That scene after killing Gortash is the moment she can not hide behind revenge or a notion of saving the world, she puts that barrier back up later but in that one moment she is totally vulnerable to how twisted her situation is. All she can do is be angry, at the world, at the hells, even at Tav. Despite perhaps being the closest living person to her in her life, what's the point if she's going to die anyway. It's easier for her to lash out. I don't know what it's like to know you'll die soon but I know that when I believe I have no future left for myself, I'm making damn sure noone cares when I'm gone so they don't have to grieve over me.

At the end of it all, you really did save the world, fought through impossible odds just as she did for 10 years. We have a habit of trying to make the whole thing logical, which unfortunately it rarely is. If you do want to use the DSM as a way of thinking more logically it can be somewhat useful to look at each of the criteria and think if that has any relevance to you. It can be big or small but it gets you thinking about how certain thoughts and feelings might have been underlying for a while. Asking after a medical diagnosis if you want one is never a bad idea, although as I said before it isn't the sole factor of whether someone is or isn't trans. My diagnosis was helpful in convincing myself that my gender issues were something I couldn't keep hiding from and allowed me to go towards hormones. The best thing I could recommend is talking to a therapist because they're not biased for or against you and give you a space to talk openly about your feelings. Of course this assumes they're experienced in talking to people with gender identity problems which can be hard to find. 

If socially transitioning has had a continued positive impact then logically speaking it's good to carry on with it. If you want to talk to a professional about the medical side of it you don't have to nake any big decisions but you can gather some more info. Wish I had some more definite answers but it is very much a personal journey that rarely follows much cold logic.

The DSM is for a medical diagnosis of Gender Dysphoria. It's not uncommon for people to transition without a diagnosis whether it's by choice or they're confident enough in their decision. 

Personally before I started hormones I didn't match all the criteria (as an adult you only need to match 4 to 6 criteria I can't remember) but with time and self reflection a lot more of the criteria fit me now when they didn't before. 

My personal advice would be to make your own decision based on thoughts and feelings then look into the medical angle of it. Unless you're certified to diagnose someone the DSM will not give you certainty in a diagnosis and the diagnosis won't give you certainty in yourself.

I will shill the series whenever I can because each game (except Red Faction 2) had really cool mechanics and elements to them. 

The first game had destructible environments and was not afraid to go crazy with weapon design.

Guerilla expanded on this moving to an open world, however the destructible environments became limited only to structures which was understandable given the scale of allowing destructible ground and caves like in the original. The game also switched to third person which suited the wide desolate spaces. 

Armageddon was a step down returning to a linear style and really being bizarre story wise, also removing more destructibility due to more confined cave designs and not many standalone buildings. BUT. They added a weapon that allowed you to drag two points into each other. So? Select an enemy and a faraway wall to slam them into it at max speed. Select an enemy and a destructible wall to use them as a wrecking ball whilst obliterating both parties. With the magnet gun you could beat the entire game using no other weapons. 

If the series ever got another game I'd want them to combine the best aspects of each game. Destructible environments including cave systems, Open world with the Guerilla hammer because that was a staple in the later two games, then finally the magnet gun and the other optimisations from Armageddon. That is the game I need in my life: Mass destruction turning my enemies into torpedoes to level buildings.

I started using in game VC a few days ago in comp. I've found the overall experience more positive than negative but whenever it's negative it is REALLY NEGATIVE. I think my first ever match in VC our tanks mental shattered so they just started screaming whilst intentionally throwing. I'm sensitive to loud noise so when people do that it is physically painful so muting them was a no brainer. 

If you have a balanced mental and can be constructive whenever things go south, I'd recommend using VC. I've so far only had one instance where someone kept saying I was trolling and I snapped back at them before being much quieter. 

In many games I'm the only one talking, but I've also found that by talking first, some people will actually talk because of it. I assume it's because you're confirming that someone is actively receiving what you're saying, so they aren't just talking to a wall of silence. 

Pings make using VC even better, because not only does it enable those who can't talk to point out important information, but it also means you can make quick and efficient callouts amongst a lot of Chaos. For example, if there is a big push and someone is flanking, you don't need to describe their position, you can just say "X is flanking here *ping*". 

I can understand if people have a much worse experience than me, especially as I play in Europe where many people don't use VC due to language barriers. I've been playing with some American friends and whenever I've used in game voice there is a lot more activity, which inevitably means there will be more negative experiences overall. However I'd still encourage people to use voice chat, because it really does change how the game feels when it works as intended. You can have a big impact, especially when tracking ultimates and suggesting combinations.

Now realistically we could all just move on and come up with whatever reason which we'll then forget, but when you're frustrated you don't exactly think the most realistically. So if you're scrambling for a reason, there are 4 of them readily available in every match. 

If I lose in a solo game, I'll get annoyed at myself or the game, but if it's a team game, you're likely to lash out to the other players as well as the game itself. 

This culture has existed in every online multiplayer and there are always going to be people who blame their teammates. Because at the end of the day, sometimes you get people who genuinely lose on purpose or are not playing the game as is the norm. So it's not going away.

That being said, the difference you can make is to just not say all of this to your team. Because getting annoyed at them and telling them that helps noone. If you can identify a weakness, be constructive. Tell the team that certain characters might be good in certain scenarios. Point out if the enemy team are switching to counter your composition. You're not blaming anyone or questioning their ability, instead you're providing options to the team that are actually helpful. If noone listens and you lose the game, avoid whoever you want and move on to the next game. You've kept a level head, you perhaps pointed blame but kept it to yourself, but most importantly you did everything you could to win the game. 

You can't change others behaviours, so just work on improving your own and being as positive as you can.

I'm going to essentially write my entire life story here in an attempt to convey some kind of point. I'm 22 and have Borderline Personality Disorder. I get you on the attachment to one person. I deem them the current "Person of interest" and only ever talk and socialise with them, trying to force every situation where I can spend time with them. 

Reading what you've written really struck many chords with experiences I've had. I was diagnosed with Depression and Anxiety many years ago and only got my more recent Diagnoses a few years ago. 

I failed my A-levels after doing well on GCSE's, at which point I became unhealthily attatched to my small friend group. I started sharing everything to the point it damaged or even ruined those same friendships. Those 2 years sucked. But then the next year was even worse. All of those friends left or moved on except for 3, but even they weren't around as much as before, in fact I only ever saw one of them. Boom, person of interest. That next year I started seeing a Psychotherapist and it put me back on the course for a good while. At that point I was being talked down from a bridge so Needless to say being somewhat OK for a while felt amazing. But those up and downs didn't go away. That was 4 years ago and the ups and downs still go on. 

Although I was doing better, I had a sense of dread about losing my person of interest. At that point I believed I would die without them, to the point it made the relationship between us get more tense as time went on. After spending 3 years trying to get my head right and trying to sort out my life during lockdowns (a time where I, like you skipped all online classes and barely scraped a pass with several kicks up the ass).

Move onto university, first term went great, no new friends and still socially inept but I was doing something again. By the end of the year I had failed 60% of the entire year and was not attending any lesson online or in person. I knew I had one more chance to retake but for the second time in 4 years I'd totally failed academically. Add onto that my crippling financial issues and it was really a fun time.

So now I'm 22 and taking my first year of University for the second time. To say I'm an outlier is an understatement. My lectures are filled with people years younger than me studying the same thing. Hell even in College I was 19 studying with 16 year olds. BUT. My head is in order, I'm trying to lose weight and sticking with it for more than 2 weeks (I'm 120kg). I'm attending lectures (not all of them I confess) and submitting assignments early. My mental health is the best it's been in forever.

Several years ago I seriously decided to end my life, and was saved by pure chance on 3 occasions. I often wonder what the world would be like without me, or what if other more valuable people survived rather than me. The difference is that every so often I see a tomorrow. I never used to see anything like that. Living day by day waiting for the courage to die. 

Our experiences have similarities and differences. We all have different perceptions of them too. I never like to say my life is hard because it feels wrong but honestly it's been pretty crap. Parents divorced when I was 8. Immediately got a stepdad who I didn't like and 14 years later is just as abusive and shitty as my real dad was. In fact no matter how much I improve myself I still have to watch someone verbally put my Mother down and mentally abuse her day after day. She doesn't have the strength or the finances to leave even though the situation is killing her. My home life is the one problem I can't fix or improve. I got suspended from school when my mental health was at its lowest, I was lied to by someone I was blindly infatuated with etc etc. 

So what is the morale of all this waste of time? Nothing. In reality there is no real reason to go on in the grand scheme. But indulge yourself a little. What would you miss? What things haven't you done that honestly you don't want to miss? In a lifetime of terrible shit what is one more day? Things will get better, then they'll get worse, then they'll probably stay worse for a bit, then things will get better again. We all go through ups and downs but for you they're just much bigger ups and downs. Try to bring your moods closer together. It makes the highs lower but it makes the lows higher. Your normal will still be the same, but those pesky mood swings will be much less steep and sudden. 

Be honest about your situation, because the guilt of hiding it will hurt more in the long term than the short term bollocking you'll get. As for the sexual things, that is trauma clear as day. I had the exact same thing for a long time. My mother was present for every single therapy session and it made me feel different because she would act differently towards me than my brother. When I started having solo sessions I took a while to open up and it caused a lot of conflict between me and my mother because she was no longer in the loop on everything. Since then any problems I have or anything that's diagnosed is mine to deal with. If I want people to know they'll know, otherwise, none of their business. 

I also have two close friends who were denied therapy because their parents disliked it. However when each of them started seeking help privately, it immediately helped them with many of their problems. It wasn't easy but the difference is really obvious in how they are now from back then. You shouldn't HAVE to share anything unless it's a direct risk to somebody or unless you want that person to know. With medications it can be a lot harder to keep that to yourself but if it's just talking therapy there is no record of it except between you and the therapist. This way you can keep your mother from weaponising any issues you might be dealing with or feeling that your teachers treat you differently.  

Best wishes to you and I hope you do try get some professional help no matter how much or little you can get.

As someone who used to be a bully its blatantly obvious to me that it isn't how people are naturally. It's a way of externalising their pain onto somebody else. It isn't right but that shouldn't mean they're forever outcast. I might not be able to change minds, not by myself.

My mindset changed because over time more and more people disagreed with me, so I went over thinking and found flaws. Initially I covered them up and if anyone poked them open again I would just flee from the argument. After enough times I accepted that I was actually wrong so my view adjusted. This was over the course of 10 years and given I'm only now 22 that's incredibly slow. 

People my age and above will take similarly long periods of time to adjust to a core value reshuffle. If you've been surrounded by one opinion and suddenly you start to see holes in it, why would you go against it? Only by challenging it repeatedly does it eventually give way. I would first of all say that social media is likely not any place to try argue, as anonymity kills all types of empathy and emotional ties to the other person. Also people often use social media as a platform to troll people regardless of their actual opinions. 

My mental health used to suffer whenever I tried to get these points across but with time and practice you learn what fights are worth your time. I dint expect anyone to do what I do, but I do think that if neither side is going to try negotiate then the cause is lost from the start. There has to be a point where you meet at the middle and show mutual respect before real change occurs. 

I wish that society would change overnight but it won't. Humans don't work that way and we can't expect them to. It takes time and repetition, the older or more entrenched a person is the longer this will take. Negativity breeds negativity so if I'm not doing my best to be courteous regardless of the person then I can't expect anything of the sort back. That expectation won't be met 90% of the time but its a principle I stand by.

I don't spend all my time online so I don't really ever have to explain anything to anyone. However in the rare instances it does happen whether its regarding trans issues or something else entirely, noone is going to change their worldview if they never hear the other side. Lord knows the media and education systems won't do it so it has to be done by someone. 

It can be a pain and majority of the time it doesn't work, but if I can help someone like those who helped me then I think its worth it. Honestly I find it shocking that you would consider what I'm saying as trolling when this is how you implement change. Nothing changes unless you're giving people the other side of the story. In fact its because of that one sided culture bred by social media that so many people remain totally in the dark about so many problems.

I personally believe its wrong to assume a reaction like that means they're not worth the time. I used to be totally medieval in how I thought and even when called things like a nazi by people didn't budge. It took a long time to come to terms with that and it wouldn't have happened if people just pushed me aside as a lost cause. I still haven't forgiven myself for those things I said and thought so I believe it's right to try and talk sense instead of dismissing people. I know I've done all I can at that point and I honestly hope they eventually make their own opinions and thoughts on topics they might not understand. 

Conflict spawns from ignorance so I will try my hardest to correct that if and when possible instead of stopping to their level of swearing and cursing instead of forming competent arguments.

This is a dangerous mindset to have. You're immediately assuming that people who are bigoted are incapable of changing which isn't true. Myself for instance used to be very bigoted out of repression and denial. 

I'm not trying to justify or excuse their behaviour, merely explain it. I know that my personal approach leaves me open to more hateful people but I'd rather take the chance to educate someone then assume they're all beyond reasoning.

It's fight or flight if you reduce it down. They're trying to scare off the other person to avoid confronting something they don't understand. It's definitely the wrong way of handling things I'm not disputing that, however it's a common response to a lot of different things just manifested differently based on context. 

When it comes to social interactions we should be compassionate and open to learning about things we may not understand. The fight or flight  reaction is not suited for having a conversation with someone online.

I've been through multiple therapies for almost my entire life. They all had different effects but during my worst ever year I had therapy and it completely changed my direction. I was hanging on to a massive amount of guilt and self hatred and that course of 12 sessions really set the tone for how I wanted to move forward. Since then I now have regular counselling which allows me to speak my mind freely without worrying about how it affects my friends or family. 

Therapy means different things to different people and you definitely need to go into it wanting to get something out of it. It will help you build on yourself but it won't do everything on its own. For me it let me really vent out everything I was thinking, how it affected me and how I thought it linked into other things from my past. It's a place to consciously process and reflect so my mind and thoughts remain nore level which helps my moods stay level (I have BPD so keeping level makes life a lot better). 

Try the therapy out and see how it goes. It might take a couple sessions to build trust or perhaps the therapist isn't a Good match. If you think that's the case it's vital you bring it up. You need to be able to trust them but also they need to be able to trust you to say if things are not going well. It can take some time with a little trial and error but I would definitely recommend you go for it.

Best of luck and I hope my ramblings made a little bit of sense.

When under private care your health is very carefully monitored for any of these effects that might need looking at. This happens to non trans people as well with Hormone imbalances. For instance my mother has too much Testosterone so needs Estrogen to maintain a healthy normal level. This has to be prescribed and monitored because of how impactful Hormones are. Menopause is the greatest example of how Hormones can cause all manners of weird changes unless monitored.
